text:
Anna M: Hey team — just got an escalation from support: customers hitting a big p99 latency regression in production after the v3.2.0 runtime canary rolled to 20%.
Josh K: ugh, details?
Anna M: We saw baseline p95 ~120ms / p99 ~1.6s. After canary p95 ~320ms / p99 ~3.2s for text-gen routes (seq_len ~512). Graphs from metrics show the jump coincident with canary start at 2112345600. Ticket: INC-9204.
Priya S: Which canary nodes? any hostnames or instance types affected more?
Anna M: Canary group: runtime-canary-3.2 (g4dn.4x) across us-west-2a/b. Top traces include kernel-selector changes and a new batching heuristic.
Miguel R: deploy-bot reported: 
```
deploy-bot: Canary rollout runtime v3.2.0 -> started (20% traffic)
changeset: 8f3a2c1..b4d9f7a
notable: kernel_selector: enable_new_selector=true, batch.autothrottle=true, kvcache_v2=true
```
Anna M: Support provided a repro curl from customer with x-request-id: r-8a3f9. Repro command they used: 
```
curl -s -X POST 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"text-large","input":"<~512 tokens>"}' -o /tmp/resp.json
```
Josh K: Can we reproduce internally? Priya, can you spin up canary image in staging and run the same load?
Priya S: On it. Spun up runtime:v3.2.0 in staging with 20% traffic emulator. Running the exact curl at 10 rps for 60s. Initial numbers: p95 310ms, p99 2.9s — yeah reproduces.
Miguel R: Stack traces? any long kernel op or memcpy hotspots?
Priya S: Trace from jaeger (trace r-8a3f9): large tail on attention kernel; context switches increased. Also saw increased time inside kernel_selector.select_path() and more frequent fallback to slower kernel.
Anna M: That points to kernel_selector change in the diff. Josh, does 8f3a2c1..b4d9f7a include the kernel selector tuning?
Josh K: Yes: commit b4d9f7a toggles the new selector. I can try flipping feature flag to false in canary group to test.
oncall-ops: FYI we should consider emergency rollback if mitigation not quick. SLA alerts are starting to trigger. :alarm_clock:
Priya S: Quick bisect plan: 1) toggle enable_new_selector=false for canary 2) if it fixes, bisect within kernel_selector changes 3) otherwise, revert batch.autothrottle and kvcache_v2 one at a time.
Josh K: Toggling flag now for runtime-canary-3.2...
```
# rollout-api
POST /rollouts/canary/runtime-canary-3.2/flags
payload: { 'enable_new_selector': false }
```

Josh K: Done. Took effect at 2112345732. Canaries now running with old selector.
Priya S: Re-running load: p95 140ms, p99 1.7s — looks back to normal range.
Anna M: Nice — sounds like new selector is the culprit.
Miguel R: Next step: bisect the selector changes. Which files touched?
Josh K: Mostly selector heuristics: selector.cc + heuristics_v2.py and a small GPU kernel dispatch tweak. I'll run git bisect across b4d9f7a..b4d9f7a^ (the selector changes span 4 commits).
Priya S: For speed, let's run two quick experiments in staging: a) revert heuristics_v2.py only; b) keep heuristics_v2 but disable dispatch tweak. If (a) fixes -> heuristics; else (b) -> dispatch.
Anna M: Support and customers need an ETA on a permanent fix / rollback plan. Can we keep canary flagged back to old selector and revert in prod?
Josh K: I'll open a PR to revert the selector commit. If tests pass, we can rollback the canary->prod rollout and then ship a corrected selector in a follow-up.
oncall-ops: Agreed. Meanwhile set route-level fallback for high-SLA customers to model variant on runtime v3.1.9 as an emergency mitigation.
Priya S: Config snippet for fallback routing in case we need to flip fast: 
```
route: /v1/generate
match: model=text-large
policy:
  - condition: customer.in_sla_list
    action: route_to runtime-v3.1.9
```

Miguel R: Also add temp throttle: reduce batch.size_max to 1 for canary to avoid batching heuristic corner cases. That will increase CPU cost but reduce tail latency.
Anna M: Support update prepared: "We identified a regression in the new kernel selector enabled in runtime v3.2.0 canary. We've toggled the selector off in canary and are preparing a targeted rollback while we bisect the selector changes. Temporary mitigations include route-level fallbacks for impacted customers and reducing batch sizes on canary nodes."
Josh K: PR #2789 opened to revert selector commit; CI currently running (unit + perf). If CI passes, I'll trigger full canary rollback to 0% and schedule prod rollback.
Priya S: Running finer perf tests to capture exact op timings. Payload: 64 warmup requests then 1000 inference requests at 5rps. Logging trace ids. Will paste flamegraphs in thread.
Anna M: Customer communication: send a short note that we mitigated and working on a fix, ETA 2-4 hours, will update.
oncall-ops: Updating incident ticket INC-9204 with timeline and actions.
Miguel R: After root cause confirmed we should add a perf unit test that runs heuristics_v2 with synthetic profiles to detect similar regressions before rollout.
Josh K: Agreed. Also adding canary perf gate: run p95/p99 microbench on representative seq lengths before advancing traffic.
Priya S: Flamegraph snippet (reduced): 
```
0.00 - 0.35 select_path()
0.35 - 0.70 fallback_dispatch()
0.70 - 1.00 attention_kernel_slow
```

Anna M: Thanks all. I'll coordinate comms with support and keep the customers posted. If anyone sees a sudden SLA alert spike, ping the incident channel and tag @oncall-ops. :thumbsup:
Miguel R: After rollback we should run the new selector in isolated perf env and run long-tail tests. Do not promote to prod until we have perf gate.
Josh K: Logging timeline:
- 2112345600 canary start
- 2112345630 first customer report
- 2112345732 toggled selector off in canary
- 2112345760 PR#2789 revert opened
- 2112345790 staging perf green for reverted config

Anna M: I'll file follow-ups: postmortem checklist, perf gate, customer comms. Closing loop here after prod rollback.
oncall-ops: Incident updated, paging closed for now.
Josh K: If anyone wants to follow bisect details I'm pushing intermediate commits to the branch bisect/selector. Ping me for access.
Priya S: Thanks team. Will attach perf artifacts to the incident.
Anna M: Great work y'all. :heart:
